bull_bear.body:
- Regulatory and Policy Risks — The education sector is highly regulated; changes in NEP 2020, digital learning rules, accreditation, or taxation could impact operations, cost structures, and institutional partnerships.
- Technological Disruption and Obsolescence — Rapid advances in AI, ML, and digital platforms require continuous investment; failure to adapt may erode competitiveness and operational relevance.
- Increasing Competition — Low entry barriers in online learning lead to market fragmentation and pricing pressure, demanding constant differentiation through quality, technology, and execution.
- Cybersecurity and Data Privacy Risks — Reliance on digital platforms exposes the company to cyber threats, data breaches, and system disruptions that could harm operations, reputation, and compliance.
- Economic Volatility and Financial Risks — Macroeconomic slowdowns, inflation, and rising costs (employee, technology, marketing) may pressure institutional budgets, discretionary spending, and operating margins.
- Talent Acquisition and Retention Risks — Attrition of skilled academic, technical, or management personnel can disrupt continuity, customer relationships, and operational efficiency in a competitive talent market.
- Geographical Concentration and Market Risks — Revenue concentration in specific regions or customer segments exposes the company to localized economic conditions, competition, and policy changes.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

outlook.body:
- Strengthen capabilities in digital learning, technology-enabled education support services, institutional partnerships, and skill development to support growth in India's education ecosystem.
- Align business strategy with e-learning, AI, and digital transformation by focusing on technology-enabled services, digital learning support, skill development, process automation, and scalable delivery models.
- Focus on skill development, training, educational services, and institutional partnerships to benefit from long-term trends in corporate training, skilling, and employability.
- The Company believes a steady dividend payout best serves the interests of the Company and shareholders, especially those dependent on regular income. It has a formal dividend distribution policy in compliance with Secretarial Standard-3 on Dividend. During FY 2025-26, an interim dividend of 25% (Rs. 0.50 per share) was declared and a final dividend of 25% (Rs. 0.50 per share) was recommended, subject to shareholder approval.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Global Education Limited is strategically preparing for the next phase of growth through value-added capabilities, new capacities, and continuous investments into productive assets to become 'future ready'. The Company incurred capital expenditure of ₹533.52 lakhs during FY26 towards Property, Plant and Equipment and Intangible Assets, mainly for expansion in the Supply of Infrastructure and Other Services operations and for enhancing operational efficiencies. Expansion strategies are devised with a risk-mitigating approach towards capex, focusing on new facilities, product launches, and online business models to support profitable growth.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's large student population, expanding higher education ecosystem, rising demand for professional education, and increasing need for employability-oriented learning continue to drive growth.
- The shift from traditional classroom-led models to blended, digital, and outcome-focused learning systems is creating demand for technology-enabled services, academic administration support, content development, digital transformation, and employability training.
- Government initiatives including NEP 2020, Union Budget 2025-26 emphasis on AI-led education, Centres of Excellence for AI, Digital Public Infrastructure, and skill development programs are expected to strengthen growth prospects.
- Growing focus on employability, industry-linked curriculum, vocational training, reskilling, and upskilling is creating demand for education support services.
- Increasing role of AI, analytics, automation, cloud platforms, and digital public infrastructure is expected to reshape the market, with education providers moving towards integrated solutions.
- Demand for corporate training, vocational education, reskilling, and upskilling continues to grow due to rapid technological change, automation, digitization, and evolving industry requirements.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

open.item: GEL continues to strengthen its capabilities in digital learning, technology-enabled education support services, institutional partnerships and skill development initiatives to support the next phase of growth in India's education ecosystem.

GEL continues to align its business strategy with developments in e-learning, AI, and digital transformation by focusing on technology-enabled services, digital learning support, skill development, process automation and scalable delivery models.
GEL's focus on skill development, training, educational services and institutional partnerships positions it to benefit from long-term trends in corporate training, skilling and employability.

For GEL, government initiatives including Viksit Bharat 2047, Union Budget 2025-26, AI-led education ecosystem, Centres of Excellence for AI, Digital Public Infrastructure, NEP 2020, skill development programs, PM Internship Scheme, National Manufacturing Mission, and Digital India provide an opportunity to strengthen offerings in educational training, business support, digital transformation, skill development and institutional services.
The Company is strategically preparing for the next phase of growth through value-added capabilities, new capacities, continuous perseverance, and inventiveness.
Expansion strategies are devised with a risk-mitigating approach towards incurring capex and making continuous investments into productive assets to become 'future ready'.
Cost efficiency programs together with strategic investments for new facilities, product launches, and launch of online business models supported profitable growth.

sk.overview: The company is positioned in the modular exhibition stands industry serving the Meetings, Incentives, Conferences & Exhibitions (MICE) sector in India. Modular exhibition stands are flexible and reusable display structures used by businesses to showcase their brands, products and services at trade fairs, exhibitions, conferences, expos and promotional events. Unlike traditional custom-built stands that are typically designed for one-time use, modular stands are made from prefabricated components that can be assembled, dismantled and reconfigured multiple times based on event requirements.
